title: Could the Midterms Be Tighter Than Expected?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Ested Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的埃斯特德·赫恩登。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: For months, Democratic Party leaders and the president himself have been bracing for huge losses in the upcoming midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，民主党领导人和总统本人一直都在为即将到来的中期选举可能遭受的惨重损失做准备。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Nate Cohn won a new Times poll that complicates that thinking and could set the stage for a very different showdown this November.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事内特·科恩发布了一项新的《纽约时报》民意调查，这项调查让这种想法变得复杂起来，并可能为今年11月一场截然不同的对决奠定基础。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, July 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月13日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, Nate, the assumption has always been, or at least it feels like this entire year has been, that the Democrats are going to get absolutely creamed in the midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，人们一直以来的假设，或者说感觉整个这一年都是这样，那就是民主党在中期选举中会彻底惨败，

sentences.en: that they'll lose seats in the House and they will probably lose the Senate as well.
sentences.zh: 他们会失去众议院的席位，而且很可能也会失去参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: But you just released a poll that takes stock of the mood of the electorate, and it seems to implicate that the picture's a little more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但你刚刚发布了一项评估选民情绪的民调，似乎暗示情况比这要复杂一些。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that poll?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们介绍一下这项民调吗？

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, we found Democrats doing, you know, not necessarily well, but maybe surprisingly well given that backdrop.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们发现民主党的表现，你知道，未必是很好，但考虑到当时的背景，可能出人意料地不错。

sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans were tied on this poll question called the generic congressional ballot,
sentences.zh: 在这次民调中，民主党和共和党在“国会选举通用投票”这一问题上打成了平手，

sentences.en: which just asks whether you'd rather see Democrats or Republicans in control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 这个问题只是问你更希望看到民主党还是共和党控制国会。

sentences.en: Among registered voters, the Democrats were up by a point.
sentences.zh: 在登记选民中，民主党领先一个百分点。

sentences.en: Among likely voters, the Republicans were up by a point.
sentences.zh: 在可能投票的选民中，共和党领先一个百分点。

sentences.en: And, you know, while usually you wouldn't say that was exceptionally good news for a political party,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，虽然通常你不会说这对一个政党来说是特别好的消息，

sentences.en: it was maybe better than you might expect, given the expectation at the beginning of this year that the Republicans were on track for a route in this year's midterm election.
sentences.zh: 但这可能比你预期的要好，因为今年年初人们普遍预期共和党将在今年的中期选举中大获全胜。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Democrats are up against headwinds that I think we know.
sentences.zh: 民主党正面临我们都知道的逆风。

sentences.en: It's hard for a new president in their first midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 对于一位新总统来说，第一次中期选举总是很难。

sentences.en: But what you're saying is that this poll actually shows that Democrats are actually still kind of in the game here.
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，这项民调实际上显示民主党目前仍然处于竞争状态。

sentences.en: Yeah, at this stage, I think it's fair to say they're still in the game.
sentences.zh: 是的，现阶段我认为可以说他们仍然在竞争中。

sentences.en: Whether they can keep it up is an open question.
sentences.zh: 他们能否保持这种状态还是个未知数。

sentences.en: But at the beginning of the race, voters are pretty evenly divided between the two parties.
sentences.zh: 但在竞选初期，选民在两党之间的分歧是相当均匀的。

sentences.en: Why do we think then, if we could guess, why are Democrats doing better than we might have expected?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们能推测一下，为什么我们认为民主党的表现比我们预期的要好？

sentences.en: One question that we ask voters is what's the most important problem facing the country?
sentences.zh: 我们问选民的一个问题是：国家面临的最重要问题是什么？

sentences.en: And it's an open-ended question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个开放式问题。

sentences.en: They can say whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 他们可以畅所欲言。

sentences.en: And in this poll, something surprising happened.
sentences.zh: 在这次民调中，发生了一件令人惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: About a third of voters chose something about guns, abortion, or threats to American democracy as the most important problem facing the country.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之一的选民选择了枪支、堕胎或对美国民主的威胁，将其作为国家面临的最重要问题。

sentences.en: But definitely the big topics of right now.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是当下的热门话题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Roe versus Wade was just overturned.
sentences.zh: “罗诉韦德案”刚刚被推翻。

sentences.en: There's been this wave of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 大规模枪击事件接连不断。

sentences.en: The January 6th committee is putting out high-profile hearings every week or two.
sentences.zh: 1月6日委员会每周或每两周就会举行备受瞩目的听证会。

sentences.en: So it's not terribly surprising that those issues are at the top of the mind of many voters.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些议题成为许多选民关注的焦点并不令人十分惊讶。

sentences.en: But it is a change from earlier in the year.
sentences.zh: 但这与今年早些时候相比确实发生了变化。

sentences.en: Earlier in the year, issues like immigration and crime and education,
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，像移民、犯罪和教育这样的议题，

sentences.en: which was sort of a grabback of different Republican resentments over race in public schools or the way the coronavirus is being handled.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是共和党对公立学校种族问题或新冠疫情处理方式不满的集合，

sentences.en: Those were the sort of issues that voters were ranking at the top of the list right after the economy.
sentences.zh: 这些是选民在经济之后排在首位的议题。

sentences.en: And that's changed with the news over the last month.
sentences.zh: 而随着过去一个月的新闻报道，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: American politics has honed in on some issues where the Democrats are on pretty good ground.
sentences.zh: 美国政治已经聚焦于一些民主党占据相当有利地位的议题。

sentences.en: And I think that's part of what's helping the Democrats solidify an important segment of the electorate that's pretty dissatisfied with the way things are going in the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有助于民主党巩固一部分对国家现状相当不满的选民群体。

sentences.en: At the same time, the issues that were expected to help Republicans at the beginning of the cycle, like immigration or crime or education and so on,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，那些在竞选周期初期被认为有助于共和党的议题，比如移民、犯罪或教育等等，

sentences.en: have become much less significant in the minds of most voters.
sentences.zh: 在大多数选民心目中已经变得没那么重要了。

sentences.en: Those three issues were only cited as the most important issue by 4 percent of the electorate.
sentences.zh: 这三个议题只有4%的选民将其列为最重要的问题。

sentences.en: So that's a much more favorable balance of issues on the top of the minds of most voters.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大多数选民心中，议题的平衡已经变得更加有利了。

sentences.en: So you're saying part of what's changed from the beginning of the year to now is the political landscape, that voters were initially talking about things like crime,
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，从年初到现在发生变化的部分原因是政治格局，选民最初谈论的是犯罪、

sentences.en: like immigration, like education, issues that maybe Republicans would prefer them to be talking about.
sentences.zh: 移民、教育等共和党可能更希望他们谈论的议题。

sentences.en: But now they're talking about abortion, guns and democracy.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们谈论的是堕胎、枪支和民主。

sentences.en: Those issues have shot up in terms of priority, according to your bullet.
sentences.zh: 根据你的民调，这些议题的优先级已经大幅上升。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And among that 30 percent of voters who choose something in that category, abortion, guns, democracy, Democrats have a big 66 to 14 percent lead.
sentences.zh: 在选择堕胎、枪支、民主这一类别的30%选民中，民主党以66%对14%的巨大优势领先。

sentences.en: So the people who care about those issues are ready to show up for the Democrats right now, whatever else they think about how the country is doing.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论他们对国家现状有何看法，关心这些议题的人现在都准备好支持民主党了。

sentences.en: What type of voter is most responsible for the bump that we've seen Democrats see in this poll relative to ones earlier in the year?
sentences.zh: 与年初的民调相比，哪类选民对民主党在这次民调中看到的增长贡献最大？

sentences.en: Well, I think that the clearest area of strength for Democrats in this poll is among white college educated voters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为民主党在这次民调中最明显的优势领域是受过大学教育的白人选民。

sentences.en: They have a considerable lead, 57 to 36 percent, which is right up there with how Joe Biden did against Donald Trump two years ago.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有57%对36%的显著领先优势，这与两年前乔·拜登对阵唐纳德·特朗普时的表现不相上下。

sentences.en: And it's easy to look into the numbers and see why.
sentences.zh: 深入研究这些数字，原因显而易见。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the likeliest group to cite abortion, guns or democracy as the most important issue facing the country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是最有可能将堕胎、枪支或民主列为国家面临的最重要问题的群体。

sentences.en: This is the most liberal group of the racial and demographic categories that we look at.
sentences.zh: 这是我们观察的种族和人口类别中最自由派的群体。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that they're most responsive when big liberal issues like abortion and guns rise to the top.
sentences.zh: 因此，当堕胎和枪支等重大的自由派议题上升到首位时，他们反应最强烈也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And they're also a relatively affluent group.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也是一个相对富裕的群体。

sentences.en: So they are maybe a little less likely to be turned off by Joe Biden's handling of the economy or inflation, which might otherwise be holding back Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能不太会因为乔·拜登对经济或通胀的处理方式而感到反感，而这在其他情况下可能会拖累民主党。

sentences.en: So it's not only that different issues have come to the forefront of the political space, but that the type of issues that are now being talked about,
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅是不同的议题已经成为政治空间的焦点，而且现在被谈论的议题类型，

sentences.en: those are issues that are specifically well suited for the type of voters that Democrats have been performing well with in recent elections,
sentences.zh: 这些议题非常适合民主党在最近选举中表现良好的选民类型，

sentences.en: college educated voters who are often or at least in a higher percentage, whiter voters.
sentences.zh: 即受过大学教育的选民，他们通常（或者至少在更高比例上）是白人选民。

sentences.en: Yeah, that group of highly educated, relatively liberal, predominantly white voter has been trending towards Democrats for a long time.
sentences.zh: 是的，那群受过高等教育、相对自由派、以白人为主的选民长期以来一直倾向于民主党。

sentences.en: And yet again, we now have another round of the news cycle that seems like it's reinforcing that trend line.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们又迎来了一轮似乎在强化这一趋势的新闻周期。

sentences.en: Have we seen the trend continue on the Republican side?
sentences.zh: 我们看到这种趋势在共和党方面持续了吗？

sentences.en: I remember doing so many stories about college educated Republican women who in the 2018 midterms were thinking about voting for Democrats or even some voters who may have thought Roe was settled law,
sentences.zh: 我记得写过很多关于受过大学教育的共和党女性的故事，她们在2018年中期选举中考虑投票给民主党，甚至有些选民可能认为“罗诉韦德案”已成定局，

sentences.en: but are now looking at a post-Roe world.
sentences.zh: 但现在她们面对的是一个后“罗诉韦德案”的世界。

sentences.en: Have we seen that transition happen on the opposite side where maybe someone who was more conservative or moderate is also thinking about or being more interested in Democrats because of the changes in politics this summer?
sentences.zh: 我们是否看到这种转变发生在另一方，即可能更保守或温和的人，因为今年夏天的政治变化，也开始考虑或对民主党更感兴趣？

sentences.en: There aren't very many voters who told us that they voted for Trump last time and are thinking about voting for Democrats this time,
sentences.zh: 告诉我们他们上次投给特朗普、这次考虑投给民主党的选民并不多，

sentences.en: but most of the people in that category tend to be college educated voters.
sentences.zh: 但该类别中的大多数人往往是受过大学教育的选民。

sentences.en: So there is this group of voters out there who the Democrats aren't their party, you know, maybe they have conservative views on economics,
sentences.zh: 所以确实存在这样一群选民，民主党不是他们的政党，你知道，也许他们在经济观点上比较保守，

sentences.en: but when national attention is focused on social issues, they're at least willing to consider the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 但当全国的注意力集中在社会议题上时，他们至少愿意考虑民主党。

sentences.en: And there are some signs of that in the poll.
sentences.zh: 民调中也有一些迹象表明了这一点。

sentences.en: But most of what we're seeing is the Democrats retaining a huge proportion of the white college educated voters who backed Biden last time.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的大部分情况是，民主党保留了上次支持拜登的绝大多数受过大学教育的白人选民。

sentences.en: And this is a midterm election.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一场中期选举。

sentences.en: You don't need to tap into too many new voters.
sentences.zh: 你不需要争取太多的新选民。

sentences.en: You can get out the people who supported you last time in a presidential race.
sentences.zh: 你只需要动员那些在总统大选中支持过你的人。

sentences.en: You're going to be in a pretty good spot.
sentences.zh: 你就会处于一个相当不错的位置。

sentences.en: And in this poll, 92 percent of the white college graduates who say they voted for Joe Biden last time are still willing to do so.
sentences.zh: 在这次民调中，92%声称上次投票给乔·拜登的大学毕业白人仍然愿意这样做。

sentences.en: And the numbers are much lower for other demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 而其他人口群体的数字要低得多。

sentences.en: So the bottom line is that in this poll, it's someone that's outlining that in a strange and what we should say kind of politically callous way,
sentences.zh: 所以底线是，这次民调以一种奇怪且可以说在政治上有些冷酷的方式指出，

sentences.en: that what Democratic voters would universally describe as really bad news this summer, Supreme Court rulings overturning Roe v.
sentences.zh: 民主党选民普遍认为今年夏天是坏消息的事情，比如最高法院推翻“罗诉韦德案”的裁决、

sentences.en: Wade, gun rulings, January 6th and the long tail of that news.
sentences.zh: 枪支裁决、1月6日事件及其后续影响，

sentences.en: It seems like that has actually maybe politically helped them among some voters.
sentences.zh: 看起来这实际上可能在政治上帮助了他们，在某些选民中。

sentences.en: I don't think you'd find too many Democratic officials who would agree to tell you this on a podcast like this.
sentences.zh: 我想你找不到太多民主党官员会同意在这样的播客上告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think that the issue landscape is better for Democrats and the Democrats are polling better too.
sentences.zh: 但是的，我认为议题环境对民主党更有利，民主党的民调表现也更好。

sentences.en: If you look at the polls that have been conducted since Roe v.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后进行的民调，

sentences.en: Wade was taken, Democrats are in the lead on average on the generic congressional ballot.
sentences.zh: 民主党在国会选举通用投票中平均处于领先地位。

sentences.en: And if you compare the polls that were taken after Roe to those from the same pollster immediately beforehand, the Democrats are doing three points better.
sentences.zh: 如果你将“罗诉韦德案”之后的民调与同一民调机构在此之前的民调进行比较，民主党的表现要好三个百分点。

sentences.en: So, you know, this poll is not alone in showing signs that the bad news, as you put it, of the last month or so has been good news for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这项民调并不是唯一显示出过去一个月左右的“坏消息”实际上对民主党来说是“好消息”迹象的民调。

sentences.en: It seems like the change in whether voters' political priorities of this summer has actually helped to at least mitigate a political fortune that looked pretty bleak.
sentences.zh: 看起来选民今年夏天政治优先事项的变化，实际上至少有助于缓解看起来相当暗淡的政治前景。

sentences.en: Yeah, what's been bad news for many Democratic voters looks like it's good news for the Democratic Party, at least for now.
sentences.zh: 是的，对许多民主党选民来说是坏消息的事情，看起来至少目前对民主党来说是好消息。

sentences.en: But the poll contains plenty of bad news for Democrats as well.
sentences.zh: 但民调中也包含了大量对民主党不利的消息。

sentences.en: And Joe Biden is one of those areas where the news will not do much to help the party's chances in the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登就是其中之一，他的情况不会对该党在中期选举中的胜算有太大帮助。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间跨越付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Nate, before the break, you said that Democrats aren't in as bad of a position as we once thought.
sentences.zh: 内特，休息前你说民主党的情况不像我们曾经认为的那么糟糕。

sentences.en: But that President Biden isn't really keeping pace with the perception of the rest of his party.
sentences.zh: 但拜登总统并没有真正跟上他所在政党其他人的支持率。

sentences.en: Can you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, the poll numbers were not good for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，乔·拜登的民调数字并不好看。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no other way to put it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有别的说法了。

sentences.en: His approval rating is at 33%.
sentences.zh: 他的支持率是33%。

sentences.en: That is lower than Donald Trump's approval rating ever was.
sentences.zh: 这比唐纳德·特朗普曾经的最低支持率还要低。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's the lowest since George W.
sentences.zh: 这是自2008年乔治·W·布什以来最低的，当时正值金融危机核心，且伊拉克战争正在进行中。

sentences.en: Bush in 2008 in the heart of the financial crisis and with the Iraq war going on.
sentences.zh: 所以这些数字对总统所在的政党来说是不利的，使得在中期选举中竞争变得非常困难。

sentences.en: So these are the sort of numbers that are not good for the president's party and make it very hard to compete in midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 现在，民主党的表现仍然比他要好。

sentences.en: Now, the Democrats are still doing better than that.
sentences.zh: 在这次民调中，他们在登记选民中获得了41%的选票。

sentences.en: They've got 41 percent of the vote in this poll among registered voters.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些选民虽然不赞成乔·拜登，但至少在民调中仍然愿意在中期选举中支持民主党。

sentences.en: So there are some voters who disapprove of Joe Biden but are still willing to back the Democrats in the midterms, at least in a poll.
sentences.zh: 但这将成为该党命运的一个巨大拖累。

sentences.en: But it's going to be a big drag on the party's fortunes.
sentences.zh: 你是说乔·拜登目前的支持率比唐纳德·特朗普任期内任何时候都要低，即使经历了两次弹劾，

sentences.en: You're saying that Joe Biden's current approval rating is lower than Donald Trump's ever was during his tenure, even through both impeachments,
sentences.zh: 即使经历了夏洛茨维尔争议，即使经历了前总统任期内发生的所有持续丑闻。

sentences.en: even through the Charlottesville controversy, even through all the ongoing scandals that happened in the former president's tenure.
sentences.zh: 他的支持率从来没有像乔·拜登现在这么低。

sentences.en: He was never at a point, approval rating-wise, as low as Joe Biden is right now.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: He never was.
sentences.zh: 现在，我必须补充一个警告，那就是你提到了两次弹劾。

sentences.en: Now, I have to add one caveat, which is that you said both impeachments.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，我并没有追踪他在2021年1月即将离任后的支持率。

sentences.en: And I got to tell you that I was not tracking his approval rating in January of 2021 after he was already on the way out of office.
sentences.zh: 所以我保留他在1月6日之后跌至如此之低的可能性。

sentences.en: So I'll leave open the possibility that he fell this low after January 6th.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: I don't remember that.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，他的表现比这要好。

sentences.en: But otherwise, he was better than this.
sentences.zh: 当他们进入2018年中期选举时，特朗普的支持率在40%左右。

sentences.en: When they were going into the 2018 midterms, Trump's approval rating was in the 40s.
sentences.zh: 他们最终还是失去了国会的控制权。

sentences.en: They still lost control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Well, how do you square that?
sentences.zh: 为什么更多的人更喜欢民主党领导国会，特别是当我们看你提到的那个通用投票问题时？

sentences.en: How is it that more people prefer Democrats to lead Congress, particularly when we looked at that generic ballot question you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 但这种亲民主党的情绪并没有转化为对民主党领袖乔·拜登的支持。

sentences.en: But that pro-Democratic feeling does not translate to support for Joe Biden, the leader of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于许多民主党人来说，他们环顾全国，认为事情进展得并不顺利。

sentences.en: Well, for a lot of Democrats, they're looking around the country, and they don't think things are going well.
sentences.zh: 就在过去一个月里，他们看到共和党可能对民主构成威胁。

sentences.en: In just the last month, they see that the Republican Party might pose a threat to democracy.
sentences.zh: 他们看到堕胎权正在消失。

sentences.en: They see abortion rights going away.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了一连串的大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: They see a spate of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们未必会因此责怪乔·拜登，但他毕竟还是总统。

sentences.en: And although they may not necessarily blame Joe Biden for that, he's still the president.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们未必会因此责怪乔·拜登，但他毕竟还是总统。

sentences.en: And so they don't approve of his job as president,
sentences.zh: 所以他们并不认可他作为总统的工作表现，

sentences.en: and they wish that he could have brought Americans together and unified the country in all the ways that he promised during the campaign.
sentences.zh: 他们希望他能像竞选时承诺的那样，团结美国人民，凝聚整个国家。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that they want to vote for the Republicans,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们想投票给共和党人，

sentences.en: who they see as trying to overturn the election as potentially a threat to the continuity of constitutional government.
sentences.zh: 因为在他们看来，共和党人试图推翻选举结果，这可能对宪政体制的延续构成了威胁。

sentences.en: So I think it's easy to imagine someone who is deeply uneasy with Joe Biden's job performance but still couldn't imagine voting for Republican.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，很容易想象出这样一种人：他们对乔·拜登的工作表现深感不安，但依然无法想象自己会投票给共和党。

sentences.en: We talked to a woman in North Carolina named Lucy Ackerman.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了北卡罗来纳州一位名叫露西·阿克曼的女士。

sentences.en: She is 23, and, I mean, here's someone who's very progressive.
sentences.zh: 她今年23岁，我的意思是，她是一个非常进步的人。

sentences.en: She recently signed up with the Democratic Socialists.
sentences.zh: 她最近加入了美国民主社会主义者组织。

sentences.en: She does not approve of Joe Biden's performance.
sentences.zh: 她不认可乔·拜登的表现。

sentences.en: But she's still as committed as ever to trying to get Democrats elected this fall.
sentences.zh: 但她依然像以往一样坚定地致力于在今年秋季帮助民主党人当选。

sentences.en: She says that she's gotten more involved to help people sign up to vote in no small part because of the court's decision to overturn Roe.
sentences.zh: 她说她之所以更多地参与进来，帮助人们登记投票，很大程度上是因为最高法院推翻了“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: Now, this is one person out of 849 people who we spoke to,
sentences.zh: 当然，这只是我们采访的849人中的一个例子，

sentences.en: but just one example of how someone can be pretty dissatisfied with Joe Biden's job and yet look around and think that Republican rule is less acceptable than ever before.
sentences.zh: 但这恰恰说明了，一个人即便对乔·拜登的工作非常不满，环顾四周后，依然会认为共和党的统治比以往任何时候都更令人无法接受。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think that if these – you can imagine a different world,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为如果这些——你可以想象一个不同的世界，

sentences.en: maybe more like the sort of situation that Barack Obama was in in 2010 or 2014 where Lucy doesn't vote because these issues like Roe versus Wade or a threat to democracy or this wave of mass shootings doesn't create that urgency that compels her to vote and that might have otherwise allowed her to be a little bit more apathetic.
sentences.zh: 也许更像是巴拉克·奥巴马在2010年或2014年所处的那种情况，那时露西可能不会去投票，因为像“罗诉韦德案”、对民主的威胁或这一波大规模枪击事件等议题，并没有产生那种迫使她投票的紧迫感，而这本可能让她变得稍微冷漠一些。

sentences.en: But those very same issues, as we were just noting, may also be hurting Biden.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们刚才提到的，正是这些议题也可能正在损害拜登的支持率。

sentences.en: So it's an odd situation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个奇怪的局面。

sentences.en: So it seems like the same factors that are mobilizing the Democratic base broadly – abortion, guns,
sentences.zh: 看起来，那些正在广泛动员民主党基本盘的因素——堕胎权、枪支问题、

sentences.en: democracy protection – are also the same issues that are making some sour on Biden because he's not speaking about these things with the same level of urgency or, frankly,
sentences.zh: 民主保护——同时也是让一些人对拜登感到失望的议题，因为他谈论这些事情时，没有表现出许多人所拥有的那种紧迫感，或者坦率地说，

sentences.en: fire and passion that many of them have.
sentences.zh: 没有他们那样的火热与激情。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There's this group of highly educated, relatively liberal voters who are not happy with Biden,
sentences.zh: 有一群受过高等教育、相对自由派的选民对拜登不满意，

sentences.en: but because these cultural and ideologically progressive issues are at stake in American politics right now, they're still going to come back to the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但由于这些文化和意识形态上的进步议题正处于美国政治的危急关头，他们最终还是会回到民主党这边。

sentences.en: The problem for the party is that there's this other group of voters.
sentences.zh: 对民主党来说，问题在于还有另一群选民。

sentences.en: They're less ideological.
sentences.zh: 他们不太讲究意识形态。

sentences.en: They're working class.
sentences.zh: 他们是工薪阶层。

sentences.en: They may care about abortion and gun control, but they care more about the economy and inflation.
sentences.zh: 他们可能关心堕胎和枪支管制，但他们更关心经济和通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And they also – not only do they not approve of Biden's performance, but they're a lot less likely to return to the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅不认可拜登的表现，回归民主党的可能性也小得多。

sentences.en: And maybe the Democrats could be losing them, not just for this midterm, but maybe even for good, given the way long-term trends are going.
sentences.zh: 考虑到长期的趋势，也许民主党不仅会在这次中期选举中失去他们，甚至可能永远失去他们。

sentences.en: This seems like an important point.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个重要的观点。

sentences.en: These are the type of voters who are less invested in politics day-to-day, who are not maybe following the every second of the January 6th hearings, and who do not know, you know,
sentences.zh: 这类选民对日常政治投入较少，可能没有关注1月6日听证会的每一秒，也不知道，你知道，

sentences.en: Nate Combe to be the polling legend that we know he is.
sentences.zh: 内特·科恩是我们所熟知的民调传奇人物。

sentences.en: But the Democratic Party still needs that type of voter to become motivated by these midterMs.
sentences.zh: 但民主党仍然需要这类选民被这次中期选举所激励。

sentences.en: What did your polling tell us about where they are?
sentences.zh: 你的民调告诉我们他们现在的立场如何？

sentences.en: The numbers weren't good for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 数据对民主党来说并不乐观。

sentences.en: You know, in fact, you know, to make a contrast here,
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实上，为了做个对比，

sentences.en: this was the first national poll or state poll with a meaningful number of non-white voters where Democrats were winning a larger share of white college graduates than Democrats were winning among non-white.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次在拥有大量非白人选民的全国性或州级民调中，民主党在白人大学毕业生中赢得的份额超过了在非白人选民中的份额。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等。

sentences.en: So this is the first poll in which the numbers for Democrats have been better with white college graduates than they have been for non-white voters.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一次民主党在白人大学毕业生中的民调数据好于非白人选民的民调？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Democrats were winning 57 percent of white college graduates in the poll compared to Democrats carrying 51 percent of non-white voters.
sentences.zh: 在该民调中，民主党赢得了57%的白人大学毕业生，而只有51%的非白人选民支持民主党。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've become accustomed in recent years to the idea that Democrats win white college graduates,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，近年来我们已经习惯了民主党赢得白人大学毕业生支持的想法，

sentences.en: but it is hard to overstate how much of a change this is in American politics in a short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 但很难夸大这在短时间内对美国政治造成的巨大改变。

sentences.en: I mean, even back in 2016, Democrats were winning non-white voters by 50 points in the race for Congress, and they were losing white college graduates.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使在2016年，民主党在国会竞选中还以50个百分点的优势赢得非白人选民，而当时他们正在失去白人大学毕业生。

sentences.en: So there has been a huge convergence of these two demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 所以这两个人口群体之间发生了巨大的趋同。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've talked at this point about many of the obvious reasons why Democrats are gaining among white college graduates.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们已经讨论过民主党在白人大学毕业生中获得支持的许多显而易见的原因。

sentences.en: But the Democratic losses among non-white voters have been going on for a long time as well, and they have continued during the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 但民主党在非白人选民中的流失也已经持续了很长时间，并且在拜登政府期间仍在继续。

sentences.en: And in our poll, it suggests it's mainly because of economic issues.
sentences.zh: 我们的民调显示，这主要是因为经济问题。

sentences.en: You know, the focus on abortion and guns democracy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对堕胎、枪支和民主问题的关注。

sentences.en: It may not hurt Democrats among those groups, but that's not why those voters are Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这可能不会损害民主党在这些群体中的支持率，但那并不是这些选民成为民主党人的原因。

sentences.en: It is not having the same role in helping revitalize Democratic support among working class and non-white voting groups.
sentences.zh: 它在帮助重振工薪阶层和非白人选民群体对民主党的支持方面，并没有起到同样的作用。

sentences.en: So we have a poll that shows, on the one hand, better overall polling for Democrats in this moment than we might expect.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在的民调显示，一方面，民主党目前整体的民调表现比我们预期的要好。

sentences.en: But they also have these very serious political challenges that they're facing, including an unpopular president and a voter coalition that shows real signs of erosion.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也面临着非常严峻的政治挑战，包括一位不受欢迎的总统，以及一个显示出真正侵蚀迹象的选民联盟。

sentences.en: What is the path forward here for Democrats?
sentences.zh: 民主党的前进道路是什么？

sentences.en: Are candidates supposed to go to voters and say, hey, you don't like the president, but you should like me instead?
sentences.zh: 候选人难道要去找选民说，嘿，你们不喜欢总统，但你们应该喜欢我吗？

sentences.en: Well, in the short term, they don't have too many other cards to play, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在短期内，他们没有太多其他牌可打，对吧？

sentences.en: Joe Biden's unpopular.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登不受欢迎。

sentences.en: The economy is not in a great place.
sentences.zh: 经济状况也不太好。

sentences.en: Unless the president can figure out a way to rejuvenate his political standing, get costs under control, help the economy and so on.
sentences.zh: 除非总统能想出办法重振他的政治地位，控制成本，改善经济等等。

sentences.en: It's hard to see them getting out of that fundamental problem.
sentences.zh: 很难看到他们能摆脱那个根本性的问题。

sentences.en: So in the meantime, they happen to have three solid issues that appeals to a really important part of their base in democracy, abortion and gun control.
sentences.zh: 所以在此期间，他们恰好有三个稳固的议题，能够吸引其基本盘中非常重要的一部分，那就是民主、堕胎和枪支管制。

sentences.en: And it's worth noting that in a midterm environment, that can get you pretty far.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，在中期选举的环境下，这能让你走得很远。

sentences.en: Midterm elections are lower turnout.
sentences.zh: 中期选举的投票率较低。

sentences.en: The electorate tends to be better educated.
sentences.zh: 选民往往受教育程度更高。

sentences.en: More ideological, consistent voters are likelier to show up in that sort of election.
sentences.zh: 更具意识形态、立场更坚定的选民更有可能在那样的选举中现身。

sentences.en: So the Democrats can get pretty far in 2022 simply by mobilizing the kind of Democratic voters who really are animated by these sort of liberal cultural issues.
sentences.zh: 所以民主党在2022年可以通过动员那些真正被这些自由派文化议题所激励的民主党选民，走得很远。

sentences.en: It may not be enough for them to hold the Congress, but perhaps if voters stayed focused on it all the way through November,
sentences.zh: 这可能不足以让他们保住国会，但如果选民能一直关注这些议题直到11月，

sentences.en: perhaps it could be enough to prevent the total wipeout that maybe you would anticipate otherwise.
sentences.zh: 也许这足以防止你原本预期的全面溃败。

sentences.en: Over the long run, that's not going to be enough, you know, for the Democrats to really, you know, win in 2024, they'll need to rejuvenate their broader coalition,
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这对于民主党来说是不够的，你知道，要在2024年真正获胜，他们需要重振更广泛的联盟，

sentences.en: not just the sort of people motivated by guns and abortion, but who care about the economy and care about bread and butter issues.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是那些被枪支和堕胎议题激励的人，还需要那些关心经济和民生问题的人。

sentences.en: Is there a tradeoff between these two voting blocks?
sentences.zh: 这两个选民群体之间是否存在权衡？

sentences.en: It seems like we're talking about two populations, a largely college-educated, disproportionately white group of folks, as we've talked about,
sentences.zh: 我们似乎在谈论两个群体，正如我们所讨论的，一个是很大程度上受过大学教育、白人比例过高的群体，

sentences.en: and a group that Democrats are eroding with on another side, which tend to be younger, which tend to be more working class, and which tend to be more non-white.
sentences.zh: 而另一个是民主党正在流失支持的群体，他们往往更年轻、更偏向工薪阶层，且更多是非白人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is there any chance that as the party focuses more on that college-educated voter in the midterms, that they hurt themselves among other populations in the long term?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能，当民主党在中期选举中更多地关注那些受过大学教育的选民时，从长远来看，他们会在其他群体中受到损害？

sentences.en: These tradeoffs exiSt. They're there.
sentences.zh: 这些权衡确实存在。它们就在那里。

sentences.en: You can think of tons of examples of it.
sentences.zh: 你可以想到无数这样的例子。

sentences.en: If you want to take climate change seriously, you wind up supporting regulations on coal that hurt you in West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 如果你想认真对待气候变化，你最终会支持对煤炭的监管，这会损害你在西弗吉尼亚州的利益。

sentences.en: In this election, I think the Democrats actually are sort of fortunate that the issues that we're talking about, like gun control and abortion and threats to democracy,
sentences.zh: 在这次选举中，我认为民主党其实很幸运，因为我们正在讨论的这些议题，比如枪支管制、堕胎和对民主的威胁，

sentences.en: don't necessarily have as many tradeoffs among the kinds of working class voters who have been supporting Democrats in recent years as some of these other newer cultural issues that the Republicans have tried to exploit.
sentences.zh: 在近年来一直支持民主党的工薪阶层选民中，并不一定像共和党试图利用的其他一些较新的文化议题那样，存在那么多的权衡。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean there's no tradeoff at all.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着完全没有权衡。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe there is something the Democrats could campaign on this election that would have a lot of appeal to working class voters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许民主党在这次选举中可以主打一些对工薪阶层选民有很大吸引力的议题。

sentences.en: But I'm a little skeptical of that.
sentences.zh: 但我对此持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: I mean, what the economy is, what it is, like, what are you going to tell them?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经济就是这样，你还能告诉他们什么呢？

sentences.en: You know, the messaging that Democrats have tried on these issues is not very good.
sentences.zh: 你知道，民主党在这些议题上的宣传并不怎么好。

sentences.en: And I get how that works from an issue level.
sentences.zh: 我明白这在议题层面是如何运作的。

sentences.en: But it does seem like when the party focuses its attention on a certain type of voter explicitly, that there is some kind of zero-sum attention choice.
sentences.zh: 但当政党明确将注意力集中在某种特定类型的选民身上时，似乎确实存在某种零和博弈的注意力选择。

sentences.en: I think about consistently all of those communities, particularly working class ones, non-white ones that we know through election cycle after election cycle,
sentences.zh: 我一直在想那些社区，特别是工薪阶层和非白人社区，我们通过一个又一个选举周期了解到，

sentences.en: often complaining about the Democratic Party that only shows up every four years.
sentences.zh: 他们经常抱怨民主党只在每四年一次的选举中才出现。

sentences.en: Isn't part of that complaint based in the fact that the party spends the midterm year focused on a different type of person?
sentences.zh: 这种抱怨难道不是基于该党在中期选举年专注于不同类型的人这一事实吗？

sentences.en: I think that's definitely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: I mean, the trend line speaks for itself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，趋势线说明了一切。

sentences.en: The Democrats have been losing ground among working class voters among all races for a decade, if not longer.
sentences.zh: 十年来，甚至更久以来，民主党在所有种族的工薪阶层选民中的支持率一直在下降。

sentences.en: And, you know, look, it's easy to say that, you know, in 2024, we'll go back to talking about working class issues or something.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，看吧，说“在2024年，我们会回到讨论工薪阶层议题”之类的话很容易。

sentences.en: But, you know, the truth is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，事实是，你知道，

sentences.en: if the Democrats don't solve these problems sooner than later and don't devise a message that will let them talk to a broader proportion of the electorate,
sentences.zh: 如果民主党不能尽早解决这些问题，不能制定出一种能让他们与更广泛选民群体对话的信息，

sentences.en: there's no reason to assume that they'll come up with it later.
sentences.zh: 就没有理由假设他们以后能想出办法来。

sentences.en: You know, it's not like the problem is they have some solution to their problem and they're not using it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，并不是说他们的问题在于他们有解决办法却没用。

sentences.en: Their problem is they don't really have a solution even.
sentences.zh: 他们的问题是他们甚至根本没有解决办法。

sentences.en: So what started off as a poll that seemed to show a Democratic bright spot seems to also show the complications of really bringing that to fruition.
sentences.zh: 所以，最初看起来显示民主党亮点的民调，似乎也显示了将其真正实现所带来的复杂性。

sentences.en: What you're describing seems to be a decision for the party that says, do we retain a college-educated, often white liberal voter who has helped us over the last 15 years?
sentences.zh: 你所描述的似乎是该党的一个决定，即：我们是保留过去15年来帮助过我们的受过大学教育、通常是白人的自由派选民呢？

sentences.en: Or do we try to win over some of the undecided ones who we also, being Democrats, need to win?
sentences.zh: 还是我们尝试去争取一些我们作为民主党人也需要赢得的未定选民？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: What do Republicans do with this type of information?
sentences.zh: 共和党人会如何利用这些信息？

sentences.en: It seems like they won't be passive actors here.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们不会在这里坐以待毙。

sentences.en: If you're the Republicans, you have a very easy hand to play.
sentences.zh: 如果你是共和党人，你手里有一手好牌。

sentences.en: And every card in your hand says Biden.
sentences.zh: 而且你手中的每一张牌都写着“拜登”。

sentences.en: My undecided voters, only 23% approve of his performance.
sentences.zh: 我的未定选民中，只有23%认可他的表现。

sentences.en: Undecided voters are much likelier to say that the economy and the cost of living is the most important issue.
sentences.zh: 未定选民更有可能认为经济和生活成本是最重要的问题。

sentences.en: Many of them do think abortion should be legal.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人确实认为堕胎应该是合法的。

sentences.en: And they are, you know, I'm sure many of them are concerned about gun violence.
sentences.zh: 而且他们，你知道，我相信他们中的许多人也担心枪支暴力。

sentences.en: And many of them think that Donald Trump acted inappropriately on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 而且他们中的许多人认为唐纳德·特朗普在1月6日的行为是不恰当的。

sentences.en: But that is not their priority.
sentences.zh: 但那不是他们的首要任务。

sentences.en: I mean, to be blunt, if these people did care that much about abortion, they would be Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，直白地说，如果这些人真的那么关心堕胎，他们早就成为民主党人了。

sentences.en: So for the Republicans, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以对于共和党人来说，你知道，

sentences.en: if they hone in on Joe Biden's job performance in the state of the economy and make a credible pitch that Republican control of Congress might be able to help,
sentences.zh: 如果他们专注于乔·拜登的工作表现和经济状况，并提出一个可信的论点，即共和党控制国会可能会有所帮助，

sentences.en: I think that they would have a good chance of winning over the preponderance of those voters.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们很有机会赢得这些选民中的大多数。

sentences.en: And suddenly that one point lead among likely voters could end up looking a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，在可能选民中那一个百分点的领先优势可能会看起来完全不同。

sentences.en: So while the Democratic card to play is to frankly try to keep the environment that we have now, the environment that you capture in the poll,
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然民主党能打的牌是坦率地试图维持我们现在的环境，也就是你在民调中捕捉到的那个环境，

sentences.en: the Republican card to play is to try to change this environment to make issues like the economy or a referendum on Joe Biden, issues they feel more confident on.
sentences.zh: 而共和党能打的牌是试图改变这种环境，让经济或对乔·拜登的公投等议题成为他们感到更有把握的议题。

sentences.en: They want that to return back to the top of voters' priority liSt.
sentences.zh: 他们希望这些议题回到选民优先事项列表的顶端。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so they'll probably, you know, take measures of their own to try and make that happen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会，你知道，采取自己的措施来尝试实现这一点。

sentences.en: And they can also just hope that the news will sort of naturally shift in their direction anyway over time as, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们也可以只是希望新闻随着时间的推移自然地向有利于他们的方向转变，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: Roe versus Wade shrinks smaller and smaller in the rearview mirror.
sentences.zh: “罗诉韦德案”在后视镜中会变得越来越小。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This could be that this poll actually captures a high watermark for Democrats because of the news cycle.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为这次民调实际上捕捉到了民主党因新闻周期而达到的最高点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you're a Republican, that's your hope.
sentences.zh: 如果你是共和党人，这就是你的希望。

sentences.en: I mean, you say, well, the Democrats just had a dream month where the national media was relentlessly focused on issues that were good for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你会说，好吧，民主党刚刚度过了一个梦幻般的月份，全国媒体无情地聚焦于对民主党有利的议题。

sentences.en: We didn't get to talk anything about immigration, crime or education, those sort of issues that we were that we thought we were going to win on earlier in the year.
sentences.zh: 我们没能谈论任何关于移民、犯罪或教育的问题，那些我们认为在今年早些时候能赢的议题。

sentences.en: And the best the Democrats can do is to more or less pull even on the generic ballot.
sentences.zh: 而民主党能做到的最好结果也只是在普选民调中勉强持平。

sentences.en: And then they can, you know, lick their chops and think about how nice it's going to be in September when they get to campaign about Biden.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以，你知道，磨刀霍霍，想着九月份能竞选拜登议题时该有多好。

sentences.en: I think it is worth stepping back to, you know, the very first point you made here, which is that the Republicans are expected to win this election.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得退一步，回到，你知道，你在这里提出的第一个观点，那就是共和党预计会赢得这次选举。

sentences.en: And there is a pretty good historical reason for that.
sentences.zh: 而且这背后有一个相当充分的历史原因。

sentences.en: When you have a president who has this kind of approval rating, your party gets crushed in midterMs.
sentences.zh: 当你的总统拥有这种支持率时，你的政党在中期选举中会被碾压。

sentences.en: There have been no exceptions, really.
sentences.zh: 真的没有例外。

sentences.en: And in this news environment, maybe we're seeing a moment where the Democrats can defy gravity for a bit.
sentences.zh: 在这种新闻环境下，也许我们正看到民主党可以暂时违背重力法则的时刻。

sentences.en: But it would be very different if they managed to defy gravity a few months from now.
sentences.zh: 但如果几个月后他们还能设法违背重力法则，那将是非常不同的情况。

sentences.en: Thank you, Nate.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，内特。

sentences.en: Appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 感激不尽。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: This is a January 4th text message from a rally organizer to Mike Lindell, the MyPillow CEO.
sentences.zh: 这是一条1月4日集会组织者发给我的枕头公司（MyPillow）首席执行官迈克·林德尔的短信。

sentences.en: In the latest January 6th hearing, congressional investigators revealed that Donald Trump planned to direct his supporters toward the Capitol, but he wanted it to look spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 在最近的1月6日听证会上，国会调查人员披露，唐纳德·特朗普计划引导他的支持者前往国会大厦，但他希望这看起来是自发的。

sentences.en: The organizer says, you know, this stays between us.
sentences.zh: 组织者说，你知道，这事儿只有我们知道。

sentences.en: We're having a second stage at the Supreme Court again after the ellipse.
sentences.zh: 我们在椭圆广场之后，还要在最高法院再设一个舞台。

sentences.en: POTUS is going to have us march there, slash the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 总统打算让我们游行到那里，冲进国会大厦。

sentences.en: Investigators also revealed that Trump attended a meeting of outside advisors who proposed to issue an executive order directing the military to seize voting machines in key swing states.
sentences.zh: 调查人员还披露，特朗普曾参加过一场外部顾问会议，会上有人提议发布行政命令，指示军方查封关键摇摆州的投票机。

sentences.en: The meeting has been called unhinged, not normal, and the craziest meeting of the Trump presidency.
sentences.zh: 这场会议被形容为精神错乱、极不正常，是特朗普总统任期内最疯狂的会议。

sentences.en: And Twitter announced on Tuesday that it was suing Elon Musk after the billionaire decided to forego his purchase of the company,
sentences.zh: 推特周二宣布，在亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克决定放弃收购该公司后，推特已对他提起诉讼，

sentences.en: setting the stage for what could be a lengthy legal battle.
sentences.zh: 这为一场可能旷日持久的法律战拉开了序幕。

sentences.en: The social media giant wants to force Musk to complete his $44 billion acquisition of the company.
sentences.zh: 这家社交媒体巨头希望强制马斯克完成他那笔440亿美元的收购交易。

sentences.en: A court in Delaware will determine whether or not Musk needs to proceed with the purchase.
sentences.zh: 特拉华州的一家法院将裁定马斯克是否必须继续完成这项收购。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko and Rochelle Bonja, with help from Michael Simon Johnson and Carlos Prieto.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科和罗谢尔·邦贾制作，迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊和卡洛斯·普列托提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by John Ketchum, Paige Cowett, and Mike Benoit, and contains original music by Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 节目由约翰·凯彻姆、佩奇·考维特和迈克·贝努瓦剪辑，并包含马里昂·洛萨诺创作的原创音乐。

sentences.en: It was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 音频工程由克里斯·伍德负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderloop.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderloop乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Estet Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是埃斯特特·赫恩登。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假日待客指南。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种喝到断片才睡着的人。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的需求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台收听《Wirecutter秀》。
